title: The home as a place of faith

opening.text: On a cold night, you can feel it before you see it. A draft slips under the door. The room is not as warm as it should be. So you seal the gap, turn up the heat and pull the family close. The house becomes a place where people want to be.
A home of faith works the same way. Some things need to be kept out. Some things need to be let in. Let us look at what that takes.

mainMessage.text: A home becomes a place of faith when we keep out what harms it and invite in what blesses it. The Spirit feels at home where there is love, prayer and trust in Jesus Christ.

blocks.text: **Seal the drafts.** Cold air gets in through small gaps. So does a sharp word or a proud spirit. If we want the Spirit in our home, we have to keep out the things that drive Him away.

For verily, verily I say unto you, he that hath the spirit of contention is not of me, but is of the devil, who is the father of contention, and he stirreth up the hearts of men to contend with anger, one with another.

President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “A Home Where the Spirit of the Lord Dwells” from the April 2019 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Contention, pride, and sin have to be kept at bay.
A few small changes can seal the gaps.
**Turn up the heat.** Sealing the drafts is not enough. A home also needs warmth. The warmth of a home of faith is the love of Christ. When it fills our hearts, the whole house feels different.
But charity is the pure love of Christ, and it endureth forever; and whoso is found possessed of it at the last day, it shall be well with him.

President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “A Home Where the Spirit of the Lord Dwells” from the April 2019 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
The pure love of Christ must come into the hearts of those in our family.
That love is the warmth we need.
**Build on solid ground.** A house in a storm needs more than warmth. It needs a foundation. A home built on faith in Jesus Christ can stand when the wind and rain come.

Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.

President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “A Home Where the Spirit of the Lord Dwells” from the April 2019 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
So building faith in Jesus Christ is the beginning of reversing spiritual decline in your family and in your home.
Christ is the foundation.
**Gather the family to pray.** In winter, a family gathers where it is warmest. In a home of faith, we gather to pray. When we kneel together and speak to God, faith grows in each person in the room.
Pray in your families unto the Father, always in my name, that your wives and your children may be blessed.

President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “A Home Where the Spirit of the Lord Dwells” from the April 2019 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
When the prayer is clearly to God in behalf of the people kneeling and listening, faith grows in all of them.
Prayer draws us in.
**A warm house takes work.** No one wakes up to a perfectly warm house. Someone has to tend it. A home of faith is the same. It is built with effort, and each person has a part.

Organize yourselves; prepare every needful thing; and establish a house, even a house of prayer, a house of fasting, a house of faith, a house of learning, a house of glory, a house of order, a house of God;
Cheryl A. Esplin, Second Counselor in the Primary General Presidency, said this in her talk “Filling Our Homes with Light and Truth” from the April 2015 general conference (General Women’s Session).
Strong eternal families and Spirit-filled homes do not just happen.
We tend the home on purpose.
**The Lord wants to stay.** A good home is a place where guests want to stay. The Savior wants to dwell with us. He promised that He and the Father would make their home with those who love Him.
Jesus answered and said unto him, If a man love me, he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him.

President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “A Home Where the Spirit of the Lord Dwells” from the April 2019 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
I know that Heavenly Father loves us, His spirit children, with a perfect love.
He loves us, and He wants to be near.

story.title: Abraham Builds an Altar Wherever He Camps

blocks.text: Abraham lived in tents and moved from place to place. But wherever he stopped, he built an altar and called on the Lord. His home moved, and his faith went with him.

And he removed from thence unto a mountain on the east of Beth-el, and pitched his tent, having Beth-el on the west, and Hai on the east: and there he builded an altar unto the Lord, and called upon the name of the Lord. Unto the place of the altar, which he had made there at the first: and there Abram called on the name of the Lord.
He made every camp a place of worship.

application.text: First, choose one “draft” to seal in your home this week. It might be a harsh tone, a screen at dinner or an old argument.
Second, choose one thing to let in, such as a short family prayer or a kind word each morning.
Third, thank God out loud for your home, however simple it is. If your home has hard days, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that a home can be a place where the Spirit dwells. I know that peace grows where Christ is welcome. I have felt that warmth in my own home. I know that Jesus Christ loves every family and wants to bless it. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: The kitchen is where a home feeds its people. Someone peels, someone stirs, someone sets the table. A meal made with care says, “You matter here.” And when the family sits down, the whole house seems to settle.
A home of faith feeds people too. It feeds the spirit. Let us look at how to cook up that kind of home.

mainMessage.text: A home of faith is made in small, daily ways. We keep out what spoils it, add what feeds it and gather often to receive it. The Lord is pleased to join us at the table.

blocks.text: **Keep out the sour.** One sour ingredient can spoil a whole pot. Contention and pride do the same to a home. If we want the Spirit at our table, we have to keep out what sours the meal.

For verily, verily I say unto you, he that hath the spirit of contention is not of me, but is of the devil, who is the father of contention, and he stirreth up the hearts of men to contend with anger, one with another.

President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “A Home Where the Spirit of the Lord Dwells” from the April 2019 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Contention, pride, and sin have to be kept at bay.
A small change can save the pot.
**Cook with love.** Food made with love tastes different. A home made with the love of Christ feels different too. That love is the main ingredient.
But charity is the pure love of Christ, and it endureth forever; and whoso is found possessed of it at the last day, it shall be well with him.

President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “A Home Where the Spirit of the Lord Dwells” from the April 2019 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
The pure love of Christ must come into the hearts of those in our family.
Love is the main ingredient.
**Start with a good recipe.** A good meal begins with a trusted recipe. A good home begins with faith in Jesus Christ. When we build on Him, we have something to return to again and again.

Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.

President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “A Home Where the Spirit of the Lord Dwells” from the April 2019 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
So building faith in Jesus Christ is the beginning of reversing spiritual decline in your family and in your home.
We begin with Christ.

**Gather at the table to pray.** The table is where families meet. Before the meal or at the end of the day, a family prayer can bring everyone together. Faith grows when we speak to God for each other.
Pray in your families unto the Father, always in my name, that your wives and your children may be blessed.

President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “A Home Where the Spirit of the Lord Dwells” from the April 2019 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
When the prayer is clearly to God in behalf of the people kneeling and listening, faith grows in all of them.
The table becomes a place of faith.
**Good meals do not just happen.** Someone shops, plans and cooks. A home of faith is made the same way. It takes thought, time and each person doing a part.

Organize yourselves; prepare every needful thing; and establish a house, even a house of prayer, a house of fasting, a house of faith, a house of learning, a house of glory, a house of order, a house of God;
Cheryl A. Esplin, Second Counselor in the Primary General Presidency, said this in her talk “Filling Our Homes with Light and Truth” from the April 2015 general conference (General Women’s Session).
Strong eternal families and Spirit-filled homes do not just happen.
We prepare the meal on purpose.
**Set a place for the Lord.** A good host sets an extra place. The Savior has promised to make His home with those who love Him. We can welcome Him each day.
Jesus answered and said unto him, If a man love me, he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him.

President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “A Home Where the Spirit of the Lord Dwells” from the April 2019 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
I know that Heavenly Father loves us, His spirit children, with a perfect love.
There is always a place for Him.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a meal or a home moment became a moment of faith. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Martha and Mary Welcome the Savior

blocks.text: Martha opened her home to Jesus. Her sister Mary sat at His feet and listened. The Lord taught that the good part is to be near Him.

Now it came to pass, as they went, that he entered into a certain village: and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house. And she had a sister called Mary, which also sat at Jesus’ feet, and heard his word. But one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her.
A home is at its best when it is a place to hear the Savior.

application.text: First, plan one meal this week where the phones are away and everyone talks.
Second, end that meal with a short prayer, spoken by someone who does not usually pray.
Third, ask each person to share one thing they are grateful for. If your family is going through a hard time, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that the Savior is glad to be welcomed into our homes. I know that He feeds us with love and peace. I have felt His Spirit at our table. I know that Jesus Christ is the center of a faithful home. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: Turn the dial on an old radio and you hear static, then a half-song, then more static. Then, suddenly, you land on the right spot. The music comes in clear. Nothing about the radio changed. It was simply tuned.
A home can be tuned like that. Some homes are full of noise. Others have found the clear signal. Let us look at what it takes to tune a home to the Spirit.

mainMessage.text: The Spirit is not far from our homes. But we have to tune out the noise and tune in to Christ. A faithful home is one that stays tuned.

blocks.text: **Turn down the static.** Arguing, pride and sin crackle like static. They drown out the signal. When we turn them down, we can hear the Spirit again.

For verily, verily I say unto you, he that hath the spirit of contention is not of me, but is of the devil, who is the father of contention, and he stirreth up the hearts of men to contend with anger, one with another.

President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “A Home Where the Spirit of the Lord Dwells” from the April 2019 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Contention, pride, and sin have to be kept at bay.
Quiet the noise and the signal comes through.
**Find the right station.** There is a station that fills a home with peace. Its signal is the pure love of Christ. When that love is in our hearts, we speak and listen differently.
But charity is the pure love of Christ, and it endureth forever; and whoso is found possessed of it at the last day, it shall be well with him.

President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “A Home Where the Spirit of the Lord Dwells” from the April 2019 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
The pure love of Christ must come into the hearts of those in our family.
The station is the love of Christ.
**Strengthen the signal.** A strong tower makes a clear signal. In a home, that strong tower is faith in Jesus Christ. A home built on Him holds a steady signal even when the storms come.

Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.

President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “A Home Where the Spirit of the Lord Dwells” from the April 2019 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
So building faith in Jesus Christ is the beginning of reversing spiritual decline in your family and in your home.
Faith in Christ is the strong tower.
**Send a clear signal back.** Radio goes both ways. We listen, and we also speak. In family prayer, we speak to God for the people in the room. Faith grows when the prayer is clear and sincere.
Pray in your families unto the Father, always in my name, that your wives and your children may be blessed.

President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “A Home Where the Spirit of the Lord Dwells” from the April 2019 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
When the prayer is clearly to God in behalf of the people kneeling and listening, faith grows in all of them.
A clear prayer builds faith.

**A clear signal takes setup.** Someone has to find the right spot for the antenna, check the wires and keep the equipment working. A home of faith is also set up with care. No one drifts into it by chance.

Organize yourselves; prepare every needful thing; and establish a house, even a house of prayer, a house of fasting, a house of faith, a house of learning, a house of glory, a house of order, a house of God;
Cheryl A. Esplin, Second Counselor in the Primary General Presidency, said this in her talk “Filling Our Homes with Light and Truth” from the April 2015 general conference (General Women’s Session).
Strong eternal families and Spirit-filled homes do not just happen.
Setup takes effort.
**The Source never stops broadcasting.** A radio only receives what is being sent. God’s love is always being sent to us. It does not stop. Our part is to stay tuned and welcome Him in.
Jesus answered and said unto him, If a man love me, he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him.

President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “A Home Where the Spirit of the Lord Dwells” from the April 2019 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
I know that Heavenly Father loves us, His spirit children, with a perfect love.
His love is always on the air.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when their home felt tuned to the Spirit. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Cornelius Prays in His House

blocks.text: Cornelius was a devout man who feared God with all his house. He prayed at home. When a messenger came, it came to a home that was already listening.

A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway. And Cornelius said, Four days ago I was fasting until this hour; and at the ninth hour I prayed in my house, and, behold, a man stood before me in bright clothing,
A praying home was ready to receive an answer.

application.text: First, find one “static” in your home you can turn down this week. It might be a loud screen or a sharp tone.
Second, choose a daily time to tune in together, such as a short prayer or a scripture.
Third, ask the Spirit to help your home feel peaceful. If you need support, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that the Spirit can fill a home. I know that He speaks quietly, and that we can learn to hear Him. I have felt His peace in my home when we turned to Him. I know that Jesus Christ is the Source of that peace. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A well in the yard is a gift. Clean it and tend it, and fresh water is always there. Neglect it and it fills with silt, leaves and dirt. The water is still underneath. But you have to clear the way to reach it.
A home can be a well too. It can hold living water, or it can fill up with things that block it. Let us see how to keep the well clear.

mainMessage.text: The water of the gospel is close to every home. We keep the well clean, we draw from it together and we trust that the source is deep. The Spirit is the water that never runs dry.

blocks.text: **Keep the well clean.** Silt and leaves cloud good water. Contention and pride cloud a home. When we clear them out, the water runs clear again.

For verily, verily I say unto you, he that hath the spirit of contention is not of me, but is of the devil, who is the father of contention, and he stirreth up the hearts of men to contend with anger, one with another.

President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “A Home Where the Spirit of the Lord Dwells” from the April 2019 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Contention, pride, and sin have to be kept at bay.
Clear the silt, and the water flows.
**Fill from the spring.** A well is only as good as the spring that feeds it. The spring of a home is the pure love of Christ. When that love is in our hearts, the whole home is refreshed.
But charity is the pure love of Christ, and it endureth forever; and whoso is found possessed of it at the last day, it shall be well with him.

President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “A Home Where the Spirit of the Lord Dwells” from the April 2019 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
The pure love of Christ must come into the hearts of those in our family.
The spring is the love of Christ.
**Dig down to rock.** A good well is dug deep, down to a strong source. A home of faith is also built deep. When we build faith in Jesus Christ, we reach something that does not dry up in a dry year.

Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.

President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “A Home Where the Spirit of the Lord Dwells” from the April 2019 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
So building faith in Jesus Christ is the beginning of reversing spiritual decline in your family and in your home.
We dig deep into faith.
**Draw water together.** At a well, people take turns drawing and passing the bucket. In family prayer, we take turns speaking and listening. Faith grows when we pray for one another.
Pray in your families unto the Father, always in my name, that your wives and your children may be blessed.

President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “A Home Where the Spirit of the Lord Dwells” from the April 2019 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
When the prayer is clearly to God in behalf of the people kneeling and listening, faith grows in all of them.
We pass the bucket together.

**Wells need regular care.** A well left alone for years will fill up. A home of faith needs regular tending. It does not take care of itself, and it does not have to be perfect. It needs steady effort.

Organize yourselves; prepare every needful thing; and establish a house, even a house of prayer, a house of fasting, a house of faith, a house of learning, a house of glory, a house of order, a house of God;
Cheryl A. Esplin, Second Counselor in the Primary General Presidency, said this in her talk “Filling Our Homes with Light and Truth” from the April 2015 general conference (General Women’s Session).
Strong eternal families and Spirit-filled homes do not just happen.
We tend it a little each day.
**The source does not run dry.** Even in a dry season, a deep well still has water. God’s love is deeper than any dry season we face. He promised to make His home with those who love Him.
Jesus answered and said unto him, If a man love me, he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him.

President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “A Home Where the Spirit of the Lord Dwells” from the April 2019 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).

His love is deeper than any drought.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when their home became a place of faith after a hard season. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Jacob Cleans His Household and Goes to Bethel

blocks.text: Jacob called his household together. He asked them to put away what did not belong and to get ready to worship. Then they went up together to build an altar.

Then Jacob said unto his household, and to all that were with him, Put away the strange gods that are among you, and be clean, and change your garments: And let us arise, and go up to Beth-el; and I will make there an altar unto God, who answered me in the day of my distress, and was with me in the way which I went.
A household got ready, and then they worshipped together.

application.text: First, find one thing that “clouds the water” in your home. Take one small step to clear it.
Second, draw from the well together. Pray or read one verse as a family this week.
Third, thank God for His love, which does not run dry. If your home needs more peace, speak with your bishop or branch president.

opening.text: A tent has no walls of stone. It is cloth and poles. Yet a tent can shelter a family through a long night, if it is staked down well. The stakes go deep into the ground. When the wind blows, the stakes hold.
The homes we live in may be small or plain or far from perfect. But a home of faith can stand like a well-staked tent. Let us look at what holds it down.

mainMessage.text: A home of faith does not depend on size or wealth. It depends on what is staked into the ground: love, prayer and faith in Jesus Christ. These hold when the wind blows.

blocks.text: **Pull out what loosens the stakes.** Stakes work loose when the ground is soft. Contention and pride soften a home. If we want the home to hold, we have to keep them out.

President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “A Home Where the Spirit of the Lord Dwells” from the April 2019 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Contention, pride, and sin have to be kept at bay.
A firm ground holds the stakes.
**Tie it all together with love.** Ropes connect the stakes to the tent. In a home, love connects each person to the others. The pure love of Christ is the strongest rope there is.
But charity is the pure love of Christ, and it endureth forever; and whoso is found possessed of it at the last day, it shall be well with him.

President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “A Home Where the Spirit of the Lord Dwells” from the April 2019 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
The pure love of Christ must come into the hearts of those in our family.
Love is the rope that holds.
**Drive the stakes into the rock.** A stake driven into loose sand will not hold. A stake driven into firm ground will. A home built on faith in Jesus Christ has firm ground under it.

Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock.

So building faith in Jesus Christ is the beginning of reversing spiritual decline in your family and in your home.
Christ is the firm ground.
**Gather inside at night.** When the wind picks up, a family gathers inside the tent. In a home of faith, we gather to pray. Prayer together draws us close and builds faith in each person.
Pray in your families unto the Father, always in my name, that your wives and your children may be blessed.

President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “A Home Where the Spirit of the Lord Dwells” from the April 2019 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).

We gather and pray.
**A tent does not stake itself.** Someone has to pound each stake and check each rope. A home of faith is set up on purpose too. It is the result of many small, steady efforts.

Someone has to set the stakes.
**The Lord stays with the camp.** A tent can be moved. A home can change. But the Lord promised to make His home with those who love Him. That promise goes with us wherever we pitch our tent.
Jesus answered and said unto him, If a man love me, he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him.

President Henry B. Eyring, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “A Home Where the Spirit of the Lord Dwells” from the April 2019 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
I know that Heavenly Father loves us, His spirit children, with a perfect love.
His love goes where we go.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when their home, however plain, felt like holy ground. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Timothy Learns the Scriptures from Childhood

blocks.text: Timothy was raised in a home that taught him the scriptures. Those early lessons stayed with him all his life.
And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus.
A home of faith plants lessons that last for life.

application.text: First, think of one “stake” your home depends on, such as a prayer or a meal together. Make it stronger this week.
Second, check one “rope” in your family. Tell someone you love them.
Third, thank God for your home, however simple it is. If you need support to strengthen your home, speak with your bishop or branch president.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know that a home of faith can stand in the wind. I know that the love of Jesus Christ is the strongest rope. I have felt the Spirit in a simple home where He was welcome. I know that He is faithful to those who build on Him. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
